_purpose: P-297 (operator ruling A-193, OPS-24 law 7): ONE row per parcel_record cell state, with the serve decision that cell state must produce on a slated rail. This file is the contract between the LDT half and the hauska-engine half of P-297: both readers consume the same rows, so they cannot disagree about what a cell state means. The LDT test is artifacts/api-server/src/lib/cellServeRule.test.ts.

_shape.name: stable row name, quoted verbatim in both repos' tests and in the P-297 close
_shape.slated: is this (county, rail) pair in the code-owned slate? The slate, NOT the county gate verdict, is the cut-over switch.
_shape.cellState: the store's own parcel_record_cell.cell_state object, verbatim, or null when there is no cell row at all. Kinds: value | absent-verified | not-applicable | refused | unaccounted.
_shape.companionRows: optional parcel_record_companion_row payloads; present on one row to prove they do not change the decision

expect.serve: cell = the cell's own answer is served; current-path = the rail's pre-cutover path runs untouched
expect.form: value | absence | refusal, or null on current-path
expect.absenceVerdict: absent-verified | not-applicable when form=absence, else null
expect.refusalCode: the reader's own refusal code when form=refusal, else null

_notCoveredHere: A `value` cell whose payload does not coerce into the rail's own domain (a negative dollar, a zero livingAreaSqft) is a declared refusal, but the coercion rule is per-rail, so it is asserted in each rail adapter's own test (P-269 does it for the dollar and structural rails in cadRollFactFromParcelRecord.test.ts). This file cannot express it without inventing a rail.

Transport failure (retrieval service unreachable, no credential). The LDT reader turns it into a refused cell carrying code `store-not-configured`, which this file already covers through the refusal rows; the transport-level row is repo-local and lives in cellServeRule.test.ts, because the engine does not read a cell over the same transport.
_pinnedRowNamesWhy: The rows a COPY of this file may not quietly drop. Adding a row is fine and expected (a reader may add one to document a state it discovered); removing or renaming one is how a fixture stops being a contract. cellServeRule.test.ts asserts this list equals its own PINNED_ROW_NAMES and that every name in it is present in rows, so the file and the test cannot drift apart.

basis.finding: no tx_rrc_well point falls within this parcel's geometry
